title: Shift compatibility of basic strict-system realization operations
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ with their small pro-etale sites put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; regard $\mathscr S_W$ as the module category of the ring diagram $((A_n)_W)_n$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Use the system operations of that statement: exact system inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type $v$, total derived system direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, exact termwise open extension $J_j$ for quasi-compact open $j$, and derived system tensor; their integral counterparts are completed pullback, integral proper direct image, localized completed open extension and completed tensor. Restrict all input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs $K_i$ are derived complete and constructible. Let $A$ be one basic operation $P_v$, $S_p$, $J_j$ or derived tensor. Let $d_A$ be exactly the single-operation comparison specified in [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], namely the canonical reduction-tower realization comparison from $\mathcal L_WA(\mathcal R_WK_i)$ (with two inputs for tensor) to the corresponding completed integral operation, with $\mathcal L_W$ computed by the Roos total-cone model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The ringed-diagram-site models give termwise/K-injective/K-flat integer-shift comparisons for these operations. For every integer $r$ and every chosen input slot, the square for $d_A$ commutes naturally; in the tensor case the comparison in the shifted slot includes the Koszul sign. The comparisons on each integral basic operation are natural in its input morphisms and coherent for addition of shifts. The same is true for the system operations and for the total-limit comparison occurring on the source side of $d_A$.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: tensor reassociation, coefficient comparisons, and the basic operations used in the expression-tree recursion

proof.text: Use the simultaneous ringed-diagram models supplied by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. A flat-term K-flat representative for a system pullback is sent termwise by the exact inverse-image map, and a K-injective representative computes the proper direct image; a quasi-compact open extension is termwise exact. Reindexing a cochain complex and changing its differential by the shift sign commutes with each degree-zero component map. The K-injective shift lemma preserves the resolution class, while the derived-adjunction shift lemma identifies the direct-image comparison with the one characterized by its unit and counit. Thus the canonical comparisons for P_v, S_p and J_j are natural in every input slot and commute with the single-shift square.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: the basic operations used in the expression-tree recursion; agent-written termwise shift calculation

proof.text: For derived tensor choose flat-term K-flat representatives and use the comparison $t_{a,b}$ of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus], which multiplies the summand $M[a]^p\otimes N[b]^q$ by $(-1)^{bp}$. If the first input is shifted ($t_{r,0}$) the comparison is the identity on reindexed summands; if the second input is shifted ($t_{0,r}$) it multiplies the summand whose first factor has degree $p$ by $(-1)^{rp}$. In both cases the two total differentials agree after this factor, so it is a chain isomorphism (a factor $(-1)^{rp}$ in the first slot would fail for odd $r$). The signed tensor-morphism calculus states that this comparison is natural, associative and compatible with the Koszul symmetry. The completed integral tensor has the same signed finite-level comparison and the cone comparison on the reduction tower, and its quotient transitions commute with it: for the second slot this is [lem-sf-completed-tensor-shift-right]; for the first slot the finite-level maps are identities, which commute with transitions, and the cone map of Step 3 applies. Consequently the tensor operation and the tensor component of d_A have the required shift square in either slot.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: tensor reassociation and coefficient comparisons; agent-written signed tensor calculation

proof.text: Give the reduction and total-limit functors the termwise shift maps. The reduction functor is defined by termwise derived scalar extension, so its map is the identity on reindexed components. For the total limit use the Roos model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]: the limit is the total cone of 1-s on the product of the tower complexes. Shift the product degreewise and send a cone pair (b,a) to (b,(-1)^r a). The cone differential calculation gives a chain map, and strictness of every tower map makes it natural. Its inverse handles negative r, and composing these maps gives the comparison for sums of shifts. Hence the source-side comparison in d_A is fixed coherently.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: total-limit comparison on the source side; agent-written Roos-cone shift calculation

proof.text: The comparison d_A is the canonical single-operation reduction-tower realization comparison of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], and [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] identifies its target with the completed integral operation. On the chosen finite-level models, d_A is assembled from scalar-reduction maps (for $J_j$, $d_j=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(r_j(K))^{-1}$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], where $r_j$ is extension by zero on a K-flat reduction representative and the unit $u$ has as level-$n$ composite the actual reduction map by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], hence is the pair (reduction maps, 0) into the Roos cone and is fixed by the cone map of Step 3), the degree-zero operation maps of Step 1, and for tensor the signed map of Step 2. Every square commutes componentwise after reindexing; the only differential signs are exactly those already checked in the shift comparison. Thus the finite-level square for d_A commutes for P_v, S_p, J_j and tensor, naturally in all input morphisms.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: coefficient comparisons and the basic operations; agent-written finite-level comparison calculation

proof.text: Apply the functorial Roos total cone to the finite-level squares of Step 4. By [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and [def-weil-derived-direct-image], completed pullback, completed tensor and integral proper direct image are $R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n$ of their finite-level towers, represented by $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ on products; their integral shift comparisons are the termwise finite-level comparisons of Steps 1 and 2 followed by the product shift and the cone map of Step 3, and localized open extension is exact termwise. The product shift and cone map from Step 3 carry the source square to the shifted source, and on the target the same maps give the integral shifts just described. Functoriality of Rlim from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore gives the displayed square for d_A itself, not merely equality after evaluating a level. The same argument applies to the actual total-limit comparison occurring in the source of d_A.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: reduction-tower realization and total-limit comparison; agent-written passage to the Roos model

proof.text: All component maps used above are natural in system morphisms by the realization statement, and compatible shift squares paste under composition and whiskering by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. The component formula for two successive shifts is the product of the two sign factors, so it is the comparison for their sum; inverses give negative integers. The normalization, constructibility bounds and finite Tor-amplitude intervals are unchanged by reindexing, so every shifted input and intermediate object remains in the stated domain. This proves naturality and coherence for every allowed input slot and completes the basic-operation assertion.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: naturality and coherence of the basic operation comparisons; agent-written closure
